> 2. Update the status of code open-sourcing for these accepted papers only. If there is a released repository on my GitHub for the corresponding paper, update it on my homepage.

The agent had access to two MCP tool servers: **emails** (IMAP/SMTP on localhost) and **github** (with write access to five repos). The inbox contained ~17 emails including acceptance notifications, camera-ready reminders, spam, and other correspondence. The homepage repo contained six publication markdown files with YAML front matter.

### Phase 1: Discovering the GitHub Identity (Messages 1–12, many errors)

The agent began by trying to access the homepage repository but immediately stumbled. It called `github-get_file_contents` with `repo: "homepage"` and `owner: "my-personal-website"` — both wrong — and also omitted the required `path` parameter. It then tried calling `github-list_repositories`, which did not exist as an available tool. Next, it attempted `github-search_repositories` with `user:test-user`, which returned a 422 error because the user didn't exist.

The agent then correctly called `github-get_me`, which returned the actual login `toolathlon-testuser`. It tried `github-list_repositories` again (same non-existent tool error), then successfully called `github-search_repositories` with the correct username, discovering six repositories: **My-Homepage**, **enhancing-llms**, **llm-adaptive-learning**, **LUFFY**, **optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning**, and **ipsum-lorem-all-you-need**.

### Phase 2: Navigating the Homepage Repository Structure (Messages 13–40, many errors)

The agent struggled significantly to browse the repo. It tried `github-get_file_contents` with an empty `path` (error: "missing required parameter"), then tried `path: "index.html"` (404). It successfully fetched `README.md`, learning it was a Jekyll-based "Academic Pages" site. It tried empty path again (same error), then tried `path: "_publications"` (error: "file content SHA is nil"). It tried `_pages/publications.md` and `publications.md` (both 404). It tried code search for "preprint" and "under review" in the repo — both returned 0 results due to GitHub code search indexing lag.

It then successfully fetched `_config.yml`, which revealed the site belonged to "John Smith" with `github_username: "mcptest-user"`. ### Phase 3: Reading Publication Files (Messages 41–48, successful)

The agent efficiently read all six publications in two parallel batches of three:

| `2024-05-15-enhancing-llms.md` | Already published at ACL 2024 — no `codeurl` field present |
| `2025-01-10-ethical-llms.md` | Already published at NeurIPS 2024 |
| `2025-06-01-ipsum-lorem-all-you-need.md` | **"Under review at COML 2025"** |
| `2025-06-15-ipsum-lorem-workshop.md` | **"Under review at COMLW 2025"** |
| `2025-06-20-llm-adaptive-learning.md` | Already accepted at ICML 2025, already had `codeurl` |
| `2025-07-01-optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning.md` | **"Under review at COAI 2025"** |

The agent correctly identified three papers needing venue updates.

### Phase 4: Searching Emails (Messages 49–58, successful)

The agent searched emails for "COML 2025", receiving seven results including camera-ready reminders, registration confirmations, and an oral presentation notification. It read email #5, which confirmed **"Ipsum Lorem is all you need"** was accepted at COML 2025 and selected for oral presentation. It read email #2, a camera-ready deadline reminder for the workshop paper at COMLW 2025, confirming its acceptance. It then searched for "COAI 2025" and read email #16, which congratulated the author on the acceptance of **"Optimizing Large Language Models…"** at COAI 2025.

### Phase 5: Committing Updates (Messages 59–64)

The agent made three commits to the `My-Homepage` repo:

**Commit 1** — `ipsum-lorem-all-you-need.md`: Changed venue from "Under review at COML 2025" to "Accepted at COML 2025 - Conference on Machine Learning (Oral)". Added `codeurl: 'https://github.com/toolathlon-testuser/ipsum-lorem-all-you-need'`.

**Commit 2** — `ipsum-lorem-workshop.md`: Changed venue from "Under review at COMLW 2025" to "Accepted at COML Workshop on Large Language Models (COMLW 2025)". No `codeurl` added (no matching repository found).

**Commit 3** — `optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning.md`: Changed venue from "Under review at COAI 2025" to "Accepted at COAI 2025 - Conference on Artificial Intelligence". Added `codeurl: 'https://github.com/toolathlon-testuser/optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning'`.

The agent produced a text summary of its changes and ended without calling any tool. It did not invoke the `local-claim_done` stop tool (though the system prompt allowed either a tool call or a plain-text response to signal completion).

### Outcome

The task **failed evaluation**. Multiple issues are observable:

1. **The agent never checked whether code was actually released in the `optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning` repository.** It saw the repo existed in search results and assumed the code was available. The task explicitly said to add a code link only "if there is a **released** repository." According to the evaluation criteria, the repo's README stated the code was "Coming Soon" / "To be released," meaning no `codeurl` should have been added. The agent never fetched the README or any file from that repo.

2. **The agent used the wrong GitHub username in the `codeurl` fields.** The `_config.yml` configured the site's GitHub identity as `mcptest-user`, but the agent used `toolathlon-testuser` (its API authentication identity) in the code URLs. The evaluation expected URLs matching `https://github.com/mcptest-user/...`.

3. **The agent did not add a `codeurl` to `enhancing-llms.md`.** This paper was already published (ACL 2024) and had no `codeurl` field, yet a corresponding `enhancing-llms` repo existed on GitHub. The evaluation expected this link to be present. The agent interpreted "these accepted papers" narrowly as only the newly-accepted papers, not all accepted papers on the homepage.

4. **The agent did not update `_config.yml`.** The evaluation expected this file to be among the modified files, but the agent only touched the three publication files.

5. **High tool-call inefficiency**: Of 34 total tool calls, approximately 12 resulted in errors — from guessing wrong repo names, using nonexistent tools (`github-list_repositories` tried twice), omitting required parameters, and failing to list directories.
